editorial_contributions.text: Summary: A matchstick graph is a crossing-free unit-distance graph in the plane. \textit{H. Harborth} [``Point sets with equal numbers of unit-distant neighbors'', in: Discrete geometry, Oberwolfach, 12--18 July 1981. Tagungsbericht 31/1981. Oberwolfach: Mathematisches Forschungsinstitut Oberwolfach. 11--12 (1981)] proposed the problem of determining whether there exists a matchstick graph in which every vertex has degree exactly 5. \textit{A. Blokhuis} [``Regular finite planar maps with equal edges'', Preprint, \url{arXiv:1401.1799}] gave a proof of non-existence. A shorter proof was found by \textit{S. Kurz} and \textit{R. Pinchasi} [Am. Math. Mon. 118, No. 3, 264--267 (2011; Zbl 1216.05090)] using a discharging method. We combine their method with the isoperimetric inequality to show that there are \(\Omega(\sqrt{n})\) vertices in a matchstick graph on \(n\) vertices that are of degree at most 4, which is asymptotically tight.
